nodes.name: Hydrothermal Synthesis
nodes.procedure: 0.15 g of oxalic acid dihydrate (H2C2O4·2H2O) was dissolved in 20 mL of deionized water and then stirred for 10 min. One piece of NF (10 mm×30 mm×1.6 mm) was ultrasonically cleaned with HCl solution (1.0 M) and ethanol for 15 min. Afterward, the above solution and the pre-cleaned NF were transferred into a 30 mL Teflon-lined stainless autoclave and then subjected to hydrothermal treatment (140 °C, 6 h). After the completion of the reaction, NiC2O4 nanorods loaded on NF were obtained and washed with ethanol and distilled water several times.

nodes.description: HER performance in 1.0 M KOH after cathodic activation (three-electrode)
nodes.source_text: The HER activity was detailedly investigated with a typical three-electrode system in a 1.0 M KOH solution... Ni@Ni/NiO_x requires a low overpotential of 71 mV to reach 10 mA cm^{-2}... Tafel slope of 61.2 mV dec^{-1}... R_ct (11.8 Ω)... ECSA value of 34.3 mF cm^{-2}... nearly 100% Faraday efficiency.

The catalytic activities... were evaluated in an aqueous solution comprising 1.0 M KOH and 0.1 M Ph-CH2OH... requiring ultralow potentials of 1.309, 1.344, and 1.377 V to achieve current densities of 10, 50, and 100 mA cm^{-2}... Tafel slope of 31.1 mV dec^{-1}... R_ct (4.9 Ω)... ~99.0% selectivity... After conducting the oxidation reaction for 120 min, Ph-CH2OH is completely oxidized

nodes.source_text: there is only a 5.2% decrease in current density after successive operations for 10 h
Ni@NiO_x exhibits excellent stability with almost overlapped LSV curves after 15 successive cycles. More importantly, the high selectivity (~99%) and average Faraday efficiency (>96%)

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni@O-Ni displays only metallic Ni phase peaks at 44.5°, 51.8°, 76.4° (111), (200), (220) planes (PDF#04-0850); NiO shows additional cubic NiO peaks at 37.3°, 43.3°, 62.8°, 75.4°, 79.3° (111), (200), (220), (311), (222) planes (PDF#71-1179).
nodes.evidence_snippet: three intensive diffraction peaks located at 44.5, 51.8, and 76.4° ... (111), (200), and (220) planes of metal Ni (PDF#04-0850). New five diffraction peaks located at 37.3, 43.3, 62.8, 75.4, and 79.3° ... (111), (200), (220), (311), and (222) planes of cubic NiO phase (PDF#71-1179, Fm-3m)

nodes.characterization_summary: NiO shows peaks at 362, 528, 695, 1070 cm⁻¹ assigned to 1st-order TO, LO, 2nd-order TO, LO; Ni@O-Ni shows weak peaks at 528, 1070 cm⁻¹ indicating O-rich surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Raman peaks of the NiO pre-electrocatalyst at 362, 528, 695, and 1070 cm⁻¹ ... first-order transverse optical (TO), first-order longitudinal optical (LO), second-order TO, and second-order LO of NiO ... two weak peaks centered at 528 and 1070 cm⁻¹ are attributed to the O-riched surface

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni@O-Ni exhibits porously cuboid nanorod structure; NiO inherits cuboid nanorod structure of NiC₂O₄ with slight contraction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Ni@O-Ni pre-electrocatalyst exhibits a porously cuboid nanorod structure ... NiO pre-electrocatalyst inherits the cuboid nanorod structure of NiC₂O₄ with slight contraction

nodes.evidence_snippet: TEM image in Fig. 2c further proves the porous structure of the Ni@O-Ni cuboid nanorod with a diameter of ~1.5 μm

nodes.characterization_summary: Uniform distribution of Ni and O elements over Ni@O-Ni pre-electrocatalyst.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Energy-dispersive X-ray (EDX) elemental mapping images display the uniform distribution of Ni and O elements over the Ni@O-Ni pre-electrocatalyst

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni@O-Ni shows metallic Ni core with 2.04 Å (111) plane and low-crystallized O-Ni shell with 2.11 Å (200) NiO plane.
nodes.evidence_snippet: HRTEM images in Fig. 2e show the co-existence of metallic Ni core and low-crystallized O-Ni shell. An interplanar spacing of 2.04 Å ... (111) plane of the metallic Ni ... edge region of Ni@O-Ni shows an interplanar spacing of 2.11 Å ... (200) plane of the NiO phase

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni@Ni/NiOₓ XRD pattern matches Ni@O-Ni with no new peaks, confirming low-crystallized NiOₓ state.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the XRD pattern of the Ni@Ni/NiOₓ matches well with that of the Ni@O-Ni, suggesting the low-crystallized state of NiOₓ

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni@Ni/NiOₓ shows increased peaks at 528, 1070 cm⁻¹ and new peak at 695 cm⁻¹ assigned to NiOₓ.
nodes.evidence_snippet: two peaks at 528 and 1070 cm⁻¹ show a significant increase accompanied by a new peak at 695 cm⁻¹ which is assigned to the NiOₓ

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni@Ni/NiOₓ shows Ni 2p peaks at 852.4 eV (Ni⁰) and 856.2 eV (Ni²⁺); decreased Ni⁰ and increased Ni²⁺ vs Ni@O-Ni.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Ni 2p XPS spectra display-two peaks located at 852.4 and 856.2 eV, attributing to the metallic Ni⁰ and Ni²⁺ species ... decrease of metallic Ni⁰ peak and increase of Ni²⁺ peak

nodes.characterization_summary: O content increases from 10.8 at.% in Ni@O-Ni to 13.2 at.% in Ni@Ni/NiOₓ.
nodes.evidence_snippet: EDX spectra show that the content of the O element increases from 10.8 at.% in Ni@O-Ni to 13.2 at.% in Ni@Ni/NiOₓ

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni@NiOₓ XRD shows no new diffraction peaks versus Ni@O-Ni, indicating structural stability of NiOₓ shell.
nodes.evidence_snippet: XRD patterns of the Ni@O-Ni and Ni@NiOₓ. No new diffraction peaks are observed, indicating the stability of Ni@NiOₓ

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni@NiOₓ shows stronger peaks at 528, 1070 cm⁻¹ and emerging peaks at 362, 695 cm⁻¹ indicating NiOₓ generation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: two emerging characteristic peaks centered at 362 and 695 cm⁻¹ can be detected ... indicating the generation of NiOₓ

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni@NiOₓ shows Ni²⁺ peak at 856.2 eV with satellite at 861.3 eV; metallic Ni⁰ peak disappears.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Ni 2p XPS spectrum of Ni@NiOₓ shows a Ni²⁺ peak located at 856.2 eV with a satellite peak at 861.3 eV ... disappearance of the metallic Ni⁰ peak

nodes.characterization_summary: In-situ Raman shows reversible transformation Ni²⁺-Oₓ ↔ γ-Ni³⁺-OOH with peaks at 476, 556 cm⁻¹ (E_g, A_{1g} Ni-O) at ≥1.35 V vs RHE.
nodes.evidence_snippet: two emerging Raman peaks at 476 and 556 cm⁻¹ ... E_g (bending vibration) and A_{1g} (stretching vibration) modes of the Ni-O bond ... γ-Ni³⁺-OOH species

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni@Ni/NiOₓ shows charge transfer resistance R_ct = 11.8 Ω, much smaller than NiO (112.1 Ω).
